messages:
alex: Heads-up: hit a weird failure mode when an auth refresh happens mid-stream. Client sees the stream hang then EPIPE once upstream closes. Repro steps below.

mira: Can you paste the repro? Is this in hosted or dedicated env?

alex: Hosted staging. Quick repro:
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <short-lived>' https://frontdoor.redwood/api/v1/stream -d @payload.json
# refresh token on auth service while stream active -> stalls
```
Stream keeps yielding and then abruptly dies when the upstream rejects the refreshed token.

sam: We validate tokens at accept by default. If token expires midstream we either have to 1) block new data until auth-refresh completes (adds latency) or 2) let the stream continue and rely on upstream to re-validate per-chunk.

ingrid: Yep. Two high-level patterns:
- eager-gate: frontdoor pauses acceptance of new client frames until auth refresh completes. Simple semantics, consistent enforcement, but increases P99 latency and ties connection slots to auth service latency.
- delegated-pass: frontdoor forwards frames with a short-lived ephemeral lease token (or original auth header marked) and marks the request as auth-delegated. Upstream must honor that. Lower latency, but moves security surface and complicates observability/rollback.

alex: Observed problem is that when upstream rejects midstream we have no good resume semantics. Client thinks it's an upstream disconnect. We could use a resume token in trailers, but that requires upstream cooperation.

sam: Also think about idempotency. For streaming writes (eg. data ingestion) a resumed attempt can double-deliver. We need a clear boundary: where retries are safe. We should specify retry semantics per-route: stream_read (safe to resume), stream_write (no automatic retry), or transactional.

mira: Could we combine: default to eager-gate for write-heavy routes and provide config flag for read-only conversational endpoints to use delegated-pass? That seems pragmatic.

ingrid: Implementation sketch:
- new frontdoor config: auth_delegation: "deny|eager_gate|delegate_lease"
- lease token TTL short (5s) and attached as x-rdwl-lease header when delegated
- streaming-resume-token: optional trailer produced by upstream to allow client-initiated resume
- add metrics: delegated_auth_count, lease_failures, midstream_rejects

alex: Tradeoffs called out: delegate_lease reduces tail latency & connection pressure but requires rollout across model-serving fleet and KMS trust. eager_gate is safe but will raise p99s under auth-service flaps.

sam: Also need to think about abort propagation. If frontdoor buffers while auth refresh in progress, should client-visible timeout start at connection or after auth gate passes? I favor starting at accept; otherwise you leak confusing client timeouts.

mira: Ops considerations: how do we test? Plan: 1) unit tests for header propagation, 2) integration test with auth service simulated slow refresh, 3) chaos test in staging toggling auth_delegation.

ingrid: I'll draft an RFC section for the config schema + rollout plan. Include sequence diagrams for both modes and backwards-compatible header names.

alex: Action items:
- ingrid: RFC section + diagrams (ETA: EOD Thurs)
- sam: list of routes that must default to eager (ETA: Wed)
- mira: test harness for auth-flap integration test (ETA: Fri)
- alex: follow up on upstream resume-trailer support with model-serving team

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled to staging for canary tests on auth-delegation feature flag (channel: #eng-ml) :rocket:

alex: Thanks — let's keep this tight. If we pick delegate_lease we need a small P0 security review re: token replay risk.
